newsitem.title: UK: Average rate options make slow start on LME.
newsitem.headline: Average rate options make slow start on LME.

text.p: Traded average rate options (TAPOs) made a slow start on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Monday, although this matched the overall trend in options, traders said.
Today is the first day of trading TAPOS in copper and aluminium - new average price contracts that are priced off the average futures price of a whole month, rather than off a specific day.
"It has been a quiet day across-the-board...but they (TAPOS) will grow gently," one trader said.

Other traders concurred that the two new contracts had made a slow start, but given that the concept was not new - average rate options known as "Asians" have been trading OTC (over-the-counter) for several years - there was no reason for today to be marked by an upsurge in business.
"There has been some enquiry, yes, but perhaps business has just been buying TAPOs and selling Europeans. We did not really expect the floodgates to open today," another trader said.

Traders said the prospects for TAPOS were difficult to gauge. The strike prices for the new options will be identical to existing traded options, whereas the current OTC average rate options have irregular strikes, tied to cents/lb, which do not equate exactly to the dollar/tonne strike.
Many users may prefer to run with their current OTC strikes, while others may switch to the LME instruments, which will be exchange-cleared by the London Clearing House (LCH)
"It may come down to what individual departments decide, and whether they are authorised to trade OTC or not," another trader added.

Also, many buyers of average rate options trade them in quarter-year or half-year strips. But most traders say the inherent advantages of TAPOS will result in a good take-up. Exercise is automatic on the last business day of the month, and contracts will be settled in cash.
Also, because TAPOs are now LME contracts, they can be classed as foreign exchange-traded options, and can be offered for sale in the U.S.

The LME has said that once copper and aluminium are trading successfully, TAPOS for the other metals will be considered. It will also consider quarterly, yearly average and more exotic contracts if there is a strong demand from the metals industry.
